output.myth: When a fisher is drowned, his widow flies the Split-Tail alone on the first calm day. It is a kite with two long tails, and they never pull together. One tail is for the house she keeps, the other for the man who went out in the boat. Ennu cut the first one from his own shirt, and Tavo came down the cliff laughing to tear it, but it would not tear, because grief is heavier than any gale. So Tavo let it go, and it climbed. Hesk saw it at the pole and wound a little slack into the string, which is why the tails reach so far. The widow ties her knot where the tails part, and lets out line until her hands go numb. Then she stops. She does not cut the string; Aun did that once and it was enough. She winds the kite home, mends her nets, and leaves the tails hanging on the peg.
output.verse:
Two tails, one knot still,
she lets the grey line run out,
tails hang on the peg.
